subject: Chemistry

source.publisher: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
source.licence: Government publication; structure + our own wording only

units.title: Domain A: Nature of Science in Chemistry

outcomes.text: Define chemistry as the study of matter, its properties and its interactions.
Give examples of chemistry sub-fields and interdisciplinary fields.
Write key questions that different branches of chemistry try to answer.
Tell science, technology and engineering apart using examples.
Define matter as anything with mass that takes up space.
State how solids, liquids and gases differ in density, compressibility and fluidity.
Recognise a state as a distinct form of matter, including plasma and exotic states.
Explain allotropes of solids such as diamond, graphite and fullerenes.
Explain how elements, compounds and mixtures differ.
Identify solutions, colloids and suspensions with an example of each.
Explain how temperature changes solubility and makes saturated or unsaturated solutions.
Describe the atom as a nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
State that shells are electron energy levels, higher for larger shells.
State that electron paths are probabilistic, not fixed orbits.
Explain that strong nuclear force holds the nucleus together.
Explain that an atomic model is a tool for understanding atoms.
State the relative charges and masses of electrons, protons and neutrons.
Link a particle type to its mass and charge.
Sketch how charged particles bend in a uniform electric field.
Define proton (atomic) number.
Explain that proton number is unique to an element and orders the periodic table.
State that radioactivity can change proton number and so the element.
Define nucleon (mass) number as protons plus neutrons.
Define isotopes as atoms with equal protons but different neutrons.
State that isotopes change mass but not chemical properties.
Work out protons and neutrons in given isotopes.
Define relative atomic mass against one twelfth of carbon-12.
State that some isotopes are radioactive.
Discuss uses of isotopes such as carbon dating and medical imaging.
Describe how atoms form cations and anions.
Read and write symbols for atoms and ions.
Calculate relative atomic mass from isotope masses and abundances.
Practise relative atomic mass calculations with given data.
Explain how noble gas configurations, octet and duplet rules drive bonding.
Compare how cations and anions form.
Account for metals being electropositive and non-metals electronegative.
Define ionic, covalent, coordinate covalent and metallic bonds.
Distinguish ionic from covalent compounds.
Draw ionic and covalent structures with dot-and-cross and Lewis diagrams.
Explain compound properties from bonding and structure.
Compare strength and conductivity of materials by their bonding.
Link strength of attraction forces to melting and boiling points.
Justify when free electrons or ions allow electrical conduction.
Recognise that some substances ionise in water.
Justify uses of graphite, diamond and metals in industry.
State formulae of common elements and compounds.
Define molecular formula.
Define empirical formula.
Deduce name and formula of a binary ionic compound from its ions.
Deduce a molecular formula from a given structure.
Use the link between amount in moles, mass, molar mass and number of particles.
Define the mole using Avogadro number.
Explain the mole and Avogadro constant relationship.
Write chemical and ionic equations for reactants forming products.
Write balanced symbol equations with state symbols.
Define redox as oxidation and reduction happening together.
Describe oxidation and reduction using electron transfer and oxidation numbers.
Identify oxidising and reducing agents.
Spot redox by colour changes with acidified reagents.
Recognise that free elements have oxidation number zero.
Derive ionic formulae from ion charges and oxidation numbers.
Identify that a monatomic ion has oxidation number equal to its charge.
Explain that oxidation numbers in a neutral compound sum to zero.
Explain that oxidation numbers in an ion sum to its charge.
Define corrosion and discuss ways to prevent it.
Explain a chemical system and how it exchanges energy with surroundings.
Tell exothermic from endothermic reactions with examples.
State that heat change is enthalpy change and read its sign.
Define activation energy.
Explain that a catalyst changes the pathway and activation energy.
Draw and read reaction pathway diagrams, with and without catalyst.
Recognise bond breaking as endothermic and bond making as exothermic.
Explain enthalpy change as energy absorbed minus released.
Calculate enthalpy change from bond energies.
Explain respiration as an exothermic process.
Recognise reversible reactions and their symbol.
Describe how changing conditions shifts equilibrium.
State that reversible reactions reach equilibrium in a closed system.
Define Bronsted-Lowry acids and bases as proton donors and acceptors.
Recognise H+ in acid solutions and OH- in alkali solutions.
Define strong and weak acids and bases.
Write dissociation equations for acids and bases.
Recognise bases as metal oxides or hydroxides, and alkalis as soluble bases.
Describe acid reactions with metals, bases and carbonates.
Identify base reactions with acids and ammonium salts.
Define acid rain.
Discuss acid rain effects using acid properties.

units.title: Domain C: Periodic Table and Group Properties

outcomes.text: Define the periodic table as elements arranged in periods and groups.
Find the group, period or block from electronic configuration.
Link group number to the ion charge formed.
Explain why elements in a group behave similarly.
Identify trends in groups and periods such as ionisation energy and reactivity.
Use names such as alkali metals, halogens and noble gases.
Predict an element property from its group position.
Deduce an unknown element position and identity from its properties.
Describe Group 1 alkali metals as soft metals with rising reactivity down the group.
Predict properties of other Group 1 elements from trends.
Predict Group 1 reactivity order from given data.
Describe halogen trends in density and reactivity.
Identify halogen appearances such as pale yellow fluorine gas.
Explain halogen displacement reactions with halide ions.
Predict properties of halogens from given data.
Analyse thermal stability of hydrogen halides.
Describe transition elements: high melting points, variable oxidation numbers, coloured compounds, catalysts.
Describe noble gases and their unreactivity.
Explain noble gas inertness through electronic configuration.
Describe metal conductivity, malleability, ductility, melting and boiling points.
State the approximate composition of clean dry air.
State the major sources of air pollutants.
State the harmful effects of air pollutants.
Explain how carbon dioxide and methane cause global warming.
Describe sulfur role in acid rain.
Describe how nitrogen oxides form acid rain.
Explain how nitrogen oxides form in car engines and are removed by catalytic converters.
Describe ways to reduce climate change and acid rain.
Define photosynthesis as carbon dioxide and water reacting with light to make glucose and oxygen.
Analyse tools that reduce personal exposure to air pollutants.
Identify high-risk situations with long-term exposure to pollutants.
Test for water with anhydrous copper(II) sulfate.
Test water purity using melting and boiling points.
Distinguish distilled water from tap water and their lab uses.
State that natural water holds both useful and harmful substances.
Recognise beneficial substances in water.
Recognise harmful substances in water.
Explain how domestic water supply is treated.
Describe water-borne diseases and how to avoid them.
Identify water pollutant effects and how to avoid them.
Explain water scarcity in Pakistan and ways to address it.
Describe the role of fertilizers in farming.
Explain NPK fertilizers as sources of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

units.title: Domain E: Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry

outcomes.text: Describe organic molecules as straight-chain, branched or cyclic.
State that a structural formula shows how atoms are arranged.
Identify and draw structural formulae.
Interpret general formulae of a homologous series.
Define structural isomers.
Identify a functional group as the part deciding a compound reactions.
Describe general traits of a homologous series.
State that saturated compounds have only single carbon-carbon bonds.
State that unsaturated compounds have carbon-carbon multiple bonds.
State that alkanes have single covalent bonds and are saturated.
Describe alkanes as mostly unreactive except in combustion and substitution.
Define a substitution reaction.
Describe alkane substitution with chlorine as a photochemical reaction.
Write equations for making alkanes by cracking.
Explain basics of nutrition and healthy eating.
Recognise the main biomolecules: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids.
Identify carbohydrates as an energy source.

units.title: Domain F: Scientific Skills and Practical Chemistry

outcomes.text: Explain why units are standardised.
Identify SI units for physical quantities.
Combine units with prefixes for magnitude.
Justify using cm3, g and s in the lab.
Explain how tools and techniques measure quantities.
Use standard form A x 10^n.
Convert values to and from standard form.
Calculate with standard form values.
Choose apparatus to measure time, temperature, mass and volume.
Suggest pros and cons of experimental methods.
Define key terms for making chemical solutions.
Explain separation and purification methods.
Suggest suitable separation methods for a mixture.
Assess purity using melting and boiling points.
Describe tests for gases such as carbon dioxide with limewater.
Explain flame tests for common cations.
Describe how paper chromatography separates soluble mixtures.
Describe locating agents for colourless substances.
Read simple chromatograms.
State and use the Rf equation.
Explain chemical lab hazards and safety precautions.
Recognise lab chemical hazard signs.
Explain why PPE is needed and which type for each activity.
Locate nearest fire extinguisher and emergency shower.
Show awareness of lab emergency procedures.
Identify apparatus from diagrams or descriptions.
Draw, complete or label apparatus diagrams.
Explain use of common techniques, apparatus and materials.
Choose the most suitable apparatus or method and justify it.
Describe qualitative, gas and other tests.
Explain techniques that keep observations accurate.
Carry out supervised tests, including identifying metal ions.
Carry out separation and purification techniques.
Pick suitable apparatus or technique and justify the choice.
Describe experimental procedures.
Read analogue and digital apparatus with suitable precision.
Take enough readings, with repeats where right.
Record qualitative observations.
Record observations systematically in a table.
Record experiment results.
Process results to reach a conclusion or test a prediction.
Predict expected results.
Interpret and evaluate observations and data.
Process data for calculations or graphs.
Plot data with best-fit lines.
Analyse and interpret data, including graphs.
Form conclusions backed by data.
Evaluate data quality and spot anomalous results.
Identify sources of error in a design.
Assess limits of an experimental design.
Plan experiments, controlling variables.
Suggest improvements to methods or techniques.
